title: megascope questions-JSON (v2)
description: Data payload for ONE ROUND of a megascope scope. It drives assets/engine.html: a run generates only this object, injected into the engine's <script id="scoping-data"> block. Structural guarantees live here; cross-file and cross-field guarantees (S1-S15, R1-R6) live in assets/megascope.mjs, which interprets THIS file as its structural pass. Keyword vocabulary is deliberately closed — see megascope.mjs KEYWORDS. All display text supports a tiny inline markup: **bold**, `mono`, ~accent-highlight~.

formatVersion.description: Pins the contract. The engine refuses anything that is not exactly 2, loudly, instead of rendering a blank document.

meta.description: Round identity, the running scope panel, framing, constraints, context, and theme.

project.description: STABLE across every round of a scope. The round never enters this string — the engine derives the storage slug from meta.round, so a per-round suffix is not merely discouraged but unrepresentable.

round.description: Which round this file is, and what it is checked against.

n.description: This round's number. Enters the localStorage slug.

of.description: Rounds planned. Doctrine stops at 4; the schema does not make an honest fifth round illegal.

revision.description: Bump when REPUBLISHING the same n with edited questions. Enters the slug, so a rewritten round cannot rehydrate its own first draft.

label.description: This round's subject, in plain language.

prev.description: Relative path to the previous round's data file. Required when n>1, null otherwise.

prevAnswers.description: Relative path to the previous round's VERBATIM paste-back. The validator parses it. No answers file, no next round.

title.description: Header title, document title, and export title.

subtitle.description: Small uppercase label under the title. Default: 'Round n of m'.

favicon.description: One or two emoji for the header mark (and the Artifact favicon).

eyebrow.description: Small mono label above the headline. Default auto-derives from the round and the counts.

headline.description: Serif intro headline: a short, plain-language sentence.

lede.description: 1-3 sentence intro. Say what the previous round settled and what this one is for.

legend.description: Overrides the sidebar 'How to read this' note.

steps.description: The numbered process steps under the lede. Default provided, and deliverable-neutral.

overallNotesTitle.description: Heading for the free-text catch-all box.

closingAsk.description: Final line of the export. Deliverable-neutral: ask for a scope update, not a phase plan.

scope.description: The running scope panel, the readiness checklist, and what every question must point at — one array, three jobs. Exactly the five slots, in the order listed by the 'slot' enum (checked as S5).

glossary.description: Term -> plain-language gloss. Every identifier-shaped token in display text must have an entry (S14), and every entry must be used (S14). May be {} when the round uses no jargon at all.

research.description: What was researched for THIS round. Round 1 is capped light by the meta-level rule below; a technical question cannot exist unresearched (S15).

mode.description: 'light' = up to 3 parallel readers, no synthesis agent, no dossier. 'deep' = a sized fan-out with a dossier.

trigger.description: The specific things in the PREVIOUS export that opened this round: an open slot, a REJECTED id, an OWN answer, a note. Required from round 2 on.

sources.description: What the research actually read. Required (min 3) when mode is 'deep'.

constraints.description: Already-decided facts, rendered as check chips. Surfacing them here prevents re-asking.

context.description: The collapsible project-context panel. All parts optional; the panel hides itself if empty.

cards.description: An auto-fitting card grid — e.g. stages, subsystems, personas, a domain map.

blocks.description: Additional labeled context blocks, rendered in order. The 'phases' type is gone — the phased plan is no longer the fixed output.

lines.description: For 'diagram': monospace lines. ~text~ = accent highlight, **text** = bold.

theme.description: Subject-grounded personality — THE ONLY SOURCE OF PERSONALITY. Usually just an accent hex; everything derives from it. The engine is never edited per run.

accent.description: Accent color as #RGB or #RRGGBB. Drives the whole accent family in light + dark.

neutralBias.description: Subtle temperature nudge for the neutral grounds.

allOf.description: Round 1 must not make the user wait — that is the point of splitting rounds.
From round 2 on, research must name what in the previous export opened this round.

sections.description: Ordered decision areas within this round. questions[].section references sections[].id.

id.description: Short id, shown as the nav tag and as the export heading (e.g. 'A'). Unique (S2). No underscore — '__other' is the engine's reserved orphan bucket.

questions.description: This round's decisions, each pre-set to a recommended default. The cap is the pressure that makes rounds real.

scopeSlot.description: One of the five scope slots, as it stands at THIS round.

label.description: Display only — how this slot is named to the user.

text.description: Where this slot stands, in plain language. The floor matters: without it, "text":"ok" legally terminates the whole loop.

evidence.description: Which answers earned this. Grammar: r<n>:<qid> or r<n>:notes. Resolved against the saved paste-back (S10/R3) — a ref to a REJECTED or absent question fails. 'chat' is not legal.

kind.description: What kind of work this is — the deliverable is data, not doctrine. Deliverable slot only; required there once settled.

assumed.description: The only honest way to settle a slot with no user answer. When true, 'assumption' is required and evidence may be empty.

assumption.description: What was assumed and why. Surfaces in its own section of the kick-off brief.

reopened.description: Why this slot regressed settled -> open versus the previous round (S9).

allOf.description: A settled deliverable must say what kind of work this is.
kind/kindOther belong to the deliverable slot alone.
'other' has to say what it is; anything else must not carry a kindOther.
An assumption must be written down, and only an assumed slot may carry one.
A slot settled on the user's answers must cite at least one.

question.description: One decision. The four-part shape — context, breakdown, (example), question — is required by the format, not left to judgment each run.

id.description: Unique within the round (S1). Appears on the card, in the export, and in evidence refs.

slot.description: Which scope slot this question feeds. Must name a slot whose state is 'open' (S6); every open slot must be named by at least one question (S7). Together: exact cover.

context.description: Why this is on the table, in the reader's own terms. Renders first on the card.

breakdown.description: The decision broken down as simply as possible. An ARRAY, not a paragraph — decomposition is a forcing function a prose field cannot be.

technical.description: The if/then hinge: true requires 'example' and research (S15); false forbids the 'example' key entirely.

example.description: A concrete, everyday illustration. Present if and only if technical is true. With options[].detail, the only fields where identifier-shaped tokens are allowed.

question.description: The decision, stated plainly. No word cap — the fault this format fixes is long option labels, not long questions.

why.description: Why the recommendation wins, and what it costs.

switchIf.description: The runner-up condition — the sentence that lets a user override intelligently.

rec.description: The recommended default, pre-selected on load. Every key must exist in options (S4). May be ANY option, not just the first.

multi.description: If true, options render as checkboxes. Default false (single-select radio).

options.description: 2-4 concrete choices. Order matters: put the natural anchor first, recommend whichever is actually best.

allOf.description: A technical question must carry its example; a non-technical one must not carry the key at all.
A single-select question's rec is one key, not a list.

key.description: Short, unique within the question (S4). A leading underscore is banned — '__own' is the engine's reserved key.

label.description: The option in a few words. Max 7 single-spaced words, 48 chars, and none of / ; | [ ] — the export's delimiters must stay unforgeable by author text.

detail.description: One line elaborating the option and its consequence.
